fact: TechCabal reports that in April 2026 Nigeria's Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission subjected airtime lending services such as MTN's to new licensing and consumer-protection requirements.

TechCabal reports MTN suspended its airtime lending in April 2026 under a regulatory suspension linked to the FCCPC's new requirements, cutting the lending base to about a quarter of its first-quarter run rate and costing about 50 billion naira in first-half revenue.

The Central Bank of Nigeria issued an exposure draft of revised Consumer Protection Regulations 2.0 to address consumer risks from fintech delivery of financial services, with comments due 29 February 2024.

The FCCPC says the Digital, Electronic, Online or Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations, 2025 are again fully operational and enforceable after the Federal High Court upheld them on 20 July 2026.

The FCCPC says the Digital, Electronic, Online and Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations, 2025 (DEON) apply to digital money lending operators, with a regularisation deadline of 5 January 2026.

The FCCPC says it began enforcement on 21 January 2026, withdrawing conditional approval from digital lenders that missed the DEON deadline and removing them from its published register of approved lenders.

The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission said the Digital, Electronic, Online and Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations, 2025 came into effect on 21 July 2025 and set 5 January 2026 as the deadline for full compliance, with enforcement to follow.

fact: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission says its Digital, Electronic, Online or Non-Traditional Consumer Lending Regulations 2025, in force since 21 July 2025, set consumer-protection rules for all digital lenders including mobile money operators.
The FCCPC invites consumers to report unlawful or unregistered digital lenders, unfair interest rates or privacy violations to its complaint portal.
